translation.name: BSB
translation.licence_note: The Berean Standard Bible was dedicated to the public domain (CC0) on 30 April 2023. Attribution appreciated, not required.

image_generation.common_prompt: Create a vertical collectible print-card illustration for a cozy post-apocalyptic pixel-art game. Use the attached image only as a visual style and format reference, never as an edit target. Render a primitive hand-cut woodblock or linocut as deliberately chunky pixel art, strictly one-color black ink on warm fibrous birch-bark-colored paper, with uneven handmade ink coverage, bold simple silhouettes, sparse hatching, limited detail, and a heavy imperfect rectangular border. Confine the illustration to the upper 67 percent and leave the lower 27 percent inside the border as nearly empty warm paper for exact verse type added later. The subject must read clearly at small size. Include no words, letters, numbers, writing-like symbols, watermark, modern logo, photorealism, polished vector smoothness, ornate religious iconography, pulpit, or church.

prints.title: The Stranger
prints.verse: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have entertained angels without knowing it.
prints.art_prompt: An exhausted cloaked traveler stands in cold rain at night while an ordinary keeper opens a small weathered inn doorway and raises an oil lamp, inviting the stranger into shelter. The scene is humble and tender, not grand or preachy; avoid halo, weapons, menace, and despair.

prints.title: One Another's Burdens
prints.verse: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
prints.art_prompt: Two ordinary travelers on a steep ruined road lift and carry one heavy bundled load together on a wooden pole between them; one is tired and the other steadies them with a kind hand. The action must communicate sharing a burden, not forced labor; avoid weapons, chains, overseer, menace, and despair.

prints.title: The Bruised Reed
prints.verse: A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish
prints.art_prompt: Two work-worn hands carefully bind and support a bent, bruised reed beside a tiny clay lamp whose weak smoking wick is sheltered and remains alight. Show no faces or full people. Both fragile things remain alive; avoid an extinguished flame, snapped-off reed, violence, and despair.
prints.note: Short opening excerpt, identified with the conventional 'a' suffix.

prints.title: Rest for the Weary
prints.verse: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
prints.art_prompt: An exhausted traveler has safely set down a heavy pack and sleeps peacefully beneath the broad sheltering branches of an old tree. A simple cup and loaf sit nearby, and the distant road continues beyond. The traveler is safe and fully at rest; avoid a deathlike pose, grave, weapons, danger, and despair.

prints.title: The Light Shineth
prints.verse: The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
prints.art_prompt: A single bright oil lamp burns in the repaired window of a small battered roadside inn at night. Across a bleak, scarred but living valley, a few tiny distant windows answer with lights of their own while dawn faintly begins at the horizon. Avoid electric lights, a modern skyline, neon, weapons, monsters, and total despair.

prints.title: A Great Calm
prints.verse: And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.
prints.art_prompt: A small battered open boat carrying several ordinary frightened travelers has just survived a violent night storm. The wind abruptly drops, the sail hangs quiet, the waves settle around the boat, and a break in the clouds reaches calm water. Give no figure supernatural prominence; avoid halo, miracle rays, cross, weapons, shipwreck, drowning, and text.

prints.title: This Day
prints.verse: Today has enough trouble of its own.
prints.art_prompt: At first light, one tired ordinary worker repairs only the single loose plank directly in front of them on a weathered shelter. Their modest tools, cup, and one manageable piece of work are close at hand while a long distant road disappears harmlessly into morning mist. Communicate attending to today's task rather than predicting the future; avoid clocks, calendars, letters, numbers, looming danger, and despair.
prints.note: Short closing excerpt, identified with the conventional 'b' suffix.

prints.title: When Friends Fail
prints.verse: At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them.
prints.art_prompt: A solitary road-worn traveler stands at a bleak fork where several sets of footprints have departed in different directions. The traveler deliberately sets down a clenched throwing stone and opens the empty hand, choosing not to strike after those who left. Keep the figure upright and wounded but not vengeful; avoid courtroom symbols, execution, weapons, pursuers, religious iconography, and text.

prints.title: Going Out and Coming In
prints.verse: The Lord will watch over your coming and going, both now and forevermore.
prints.art_prompt: An ordinary young traveler with a small practical pack pauses at the threshold of a repaired roadside shelter at dawn. One set of footprints leads outward onto a long but passable road, while another older set returns safely to the same open doorway and warm lamp. Emphasize departure without exile and the possibility of return; avoid farewell crowd, map, signs, letters, weapons, religious iconography, and text.

prints.title: Not Comfortless
prints.verse: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
prints.art_prompt: A lone exhausted traveler sits beside a cold roadside marker at dusk, looking up as a second ordinary traveler approaches from the distance carrying a small warm oil lamp and an extra blanket. The approaching person is unmistakably real and human, and there is room beside the seated traveler. Avoid angel wings, halo, apparition, church, weapons, threatening pursuit, and text.

prints.title: Strength in Weakness
prints.verse: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.”
prints.art_prompt: Close view of an older traveler's visibly trembling, work-worn hands patiently braiding several thin fragile plant fibers into one strong useful cord. A simple walking stick rests nearby, neither hidden nor treated as shameful. Show quiet skill and adaptation rather than miraculous healing; avoid broken hands, shackles, medical equipment, religious iconography, and text.
prints.note: Short opening excerpt, identified with the conventional 'a' suffix.

prints.title: Out of the Mire
prints.verse: He lifted me up from the pit of despair, out of the miry clay; He set my feet upon a rock, and made my footsteps firm.
prints.art_prompt: A mud-covered exhausted traveler is being helped out of a deep sucking bog onto broad solid rock by the strong outstretched hand of another ordinary person just above. Both of the rescued traveler's feet reach stable stone and the next few safe footholds are visible. Emphasize practical rescue and firm footing; avoid supernatural figures, halo, bottomless abyss, skeletons, weapons, and text.
